newsitem.title: CANADA: Nova Scotia to lead Atlantic growth, bank says.
newsitem.headline: Nova Scotia to lead Atlantic growth, bank says.

text.p: Nova Scotia will lead Canada's Atlantic provinces in economic growth during the next two years, said an economic report by a large Canadian bank.

Capital project spending, a strong technology sector and modest improvements in the fisheries industry will drive economic growth of 2.5 percent this year and 3.25 percent in 1998, said the Bank of Montreal in its regional outlook.

"One of the main contributors will be construction. Capital projects, in particular construction of the Sable Island natural gas project, are bound to have a formidable impact," said Tim O'Neill, the bank's chief economist.
Capital spending projects, including C$3 billion worth of investments in the Sable Island project, are expected to employ more than 1,000 construction workers this year, the bank said.
Nova Scotia's unemployment is expected to decline from 12.7% in 1996 to 12.4% in 1997 and 11.6% in 1998, O'Neill added.
Prince Edward Island will trail all other Canadian provinces this year as the province's economy shrinks by 1.25 percent, the bank said.
But P.E.I's economy will make a comeback in 1998 with growth of 2.0 percent, the bank said.
The completion of the Confederation Bridge will initially remove a tremendous economic stimulant, in the form of non-residential building and related activities, O'Neill said.
New Brunswick's economy will grow 2.5 percent this year and 3.0 percent in 1998, while Newfoundland's economy will enjoy 1.25 percent growth this year and 3.0 percent in 1998, the bank said.
